subject: Re: Dedicated capacity RFP — slotting, GPU family recommendations, and acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@cloudforge.com>

Cc: CloudForge Procurement <procurement@cloudforge.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity RFP — initial ask and throughput targets

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Attached is CloudForge's dedicated capacity questionnaire (CloudForge_RFP_Dedicated_Sizing_v1.pdf) and a small sample of production traffic (CF-MAP-usage.csv). We're preparing a reserved pool for Q4. High-level asks:

- Target steady-state throughput of ~45k short-text generation requests/min across a mix of 1–3s response latencies for the majority of calls.
- Peak burst tolerance of ~2.5x sustained for 20-minute windows.
- Embedding workloads (512-d) at ~1200 reqs/min concurrently.
- Strong preference for multi-family fallback (A100-class and lower-cost H100/L40-like profiles).

Can you confirm: what GPU families you'd recommend, expected tokens/sec per GPU for our mix, suggested reservation sizing (committed + burst), and acceptance criteria for a staged rollout? Also include any procurement SLAs and lead times for provisioning dedicated pools.

Would appreciate a short workshop this week to align assumptions; proposed times below.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Singh

Hi Priya — thanks for the packet and sample traces. We're available for a 30-min workshop tomorrow 09:00–12:00 PT; I booked a provisional slot at 10:00 PT pending your confirmation.

High-level response up front: we generally recommend a two-tier reserved strategy for scenarios like yours — a committed steady pool sized to cover ~70–80% of steady-state, plus a burst buffer that can be invoked on demand for short windows. That minimizes committed spend while preserving headroom for the 2.5x bursts.

I'll loop Ben (SE) and Laura (AM/procurement lead) to provide a detailed GPU-family mapping and procurement timeline. Expect an initial sizing sketch + acceptance criteria in a follow-up within 24 hours.

Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity RFP — initial ask and throughput targets

Hi Priya — good session earlier. I reviewed the CF-MAP sample and sketched out an initial GPU mix and throughput table. Key recommendations (summary):

- GPU family recommendations:
  - Profile A (latency-sensitive gen): NVIDIA H100-equivalent nodes for critical low-latency pathways. Expect ~1,800–2,200 short-text tokens/sec per card depending on prompt length and quantization.
  - Profile B (cost-efficient gen + batching): A40/A10-class or 80-bit quantized H100 variants for bulk generation and embeddings. Expect ~900–1,300 tokens/sec per card under batching.
  - Embeddings: Mixed usage on B-profile nodes with isolated embedding pools sized to handle the 1,200 reqs/min (512-d) — 2 GPUs dedicated for embeddings with autoscale headroom.

- Sizing sketch (steady vs committed):
  - Steady-state target (45k reqs/min) approx maps to ~12 B-profile GPUs with intelligent batching and KV caching (70–80% load).
  - Committed pool recommendation: 9 B-profile GPUs + 2 H100-class (for latency-critical routes) to cover 75% of steady-state with 20% reserved headroom.
  - Burst buffer: additional 6 mixed GPUs (hot-standby) available for 20–30 minute windows via burst provisioning.

- Acceptance criteria for staged rollout:
  - Phase 1 (pilot, 2 weeks): baseline SLO verification — 95th p99 latency < 1.5x target for 95% of calls, tail latency budget verified under 1.5x baseline.
  - Phase 2 (scale): ramp to 50% traffic over 48 hrs and validate throughput without >1% error-rate increase.
  - Production cutover: successful run at 100% for 72 hrs with monitoring enabled and rollback guardrails tested.

- Lead times / procurement notes: typical provisioning lead time for Dedicated pools is 3–5 business days once the commitment and region are confirmed; priority slots reduce that to 24–48 hours for committed contracts. DocuSign and payment SOW finalize provisioning.

I'll attach a worked workbook with tokens/sec estimates and the assumptions used for your team to review.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Procurement checklist and SLA clarifications — CloudForge dedicated pool

Hi Alex / Priya — answering your questions and attaching a short procurement checklist plus an MSA addendum template. Short answers:

1) Tokens/sec breakdown: see tab "PromptMix" in the workbook Ben attached. For your provided prompt distribution (heavy short prompts ~60%, medium ~30%, long ~10%) the expected tokens/sec per B-profile GPU averages ~1,050 tokens/sec. We included conservative headroom in the workbook for variance.

2) Burst provisioning: fully API-driven. Customers can configure autoscale policies with TTLs (min-burst-duration, cooldown) and automated fallback to our hosted-compatible tier. Burst activation is typically instantaneous (sub-minute) for pre-warmed hot-standby GPUs; otherwise provisioning within the 24–48 hour fast-provision window if capacity needs to be allocated.

3) Emergency fill & RTO: for committed customers we offer a graded escalation — initial automated burst (hot-standby) + 1-hour remediation SLA to provide additional capacity where available; for enterprise SLA (add-on) we can commit a 30-minute RTO with higher availability credit. Exact RTO is subject to region and existing pool utilization; we'll capture the preferred SLA in the addendum.

Procurement checklist (summary):
- Sign MSA addendum (attached)
- Provide PO and billing contact
- Confirm region and initial committed pool sizes
- Agree on ramp schedule and pilot dates
- DocuSign executed -> provisioning starts (3–5 business days standard, 24–48 for priority)

Attaching: redwood-procurement-checklist.pdf and the MSA addendum draft. I'll follow up with the AM playbook for billing cadence and invoicing terms.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
